data_profile.ambiguity_note: Several label boundaries are inherently ambiguous in H&E histopathology: 'background' vs 'debris' (both may include non-specific material, artifacts, or out-of-focus regions); 'cancer-associated stroma' vs 'smooth muscle' (the invasive-front transition zone is a known diagnostic gray area); and 'mucus' (intracellular goblet-cell content vs. extracellular pools) can overlap with 'background' or 'debris'. The 'normal colon mucosa' label also lacks a defined threshold for reactive or metaplastic changes. These ambiguities are compounded by the fact that test annotations come from a different site
ambiguity_risks: Cross-center domain shift: test images (CRC-VAL-HE-7K) originate from a different clinical center, introducing uncontrolled variation in H&E staining protocol, section thickness, scanner color calibration, and slide preparation that can shift pixel-level feature distributions.

Severe test-set class-distribution shift: 'debris' drops from 10,360 (train) to 339 (test) (~30× reduction), 'smooth muscle' from 12,182 to 592, and 'cancer-associated stroma' from 9,401 to 421, suggesting different tissue composition or annotation granularity at the external site.

Test-set imbalance (max/min ≈ 3.64) is more than double the train imbalance (1.63), meaning minority classes in test (debris, smooth muscle, stroma) are under-represented relative to their training exposure, inflating variance in per-class metrics.

The 'background' class (847 test vs 9,509 train) may reflect different cropping or tiling strategies at the external center, making it unclear whether the model is learning tissue features or site-specific artifact patterns.

Annotation protocol heterogeneity: a different clinical center may apply different inclusion/exclusion criteria for ambiguous classes (e.g., what fraction of a tile must be stroma vs smooth muscle), creating label-noise that is not present in the training distribution.

The small absolute test counts for 'debris' (339) and 'cancer-associated stroma' (421) limit statistical power for reliable per-class evaluation and increase sensitivity to a handful of mislabeled tiles.
No information is provided about whether the external site used the same tile size, magnification, or preprocessing pipeline, making it impossible to rule out resolution or scale shift as a confound.

The 'normal colon mucosa' label assumes a binary normal/abnormal distinction; inter-observer variability in defining 'normal' (e.g., mild dysplasia, reactive atypia) may be systematically different across centers, introducing label drift that is invisible in aggregate accuracy.

dataset_manifest.test_domain_note: CRC-VAL-HE-7K test images originate from a different clinical center.

representation_plan.rationale: Standardize normalization mitigates site-specific staining intensity variation (test annotations from a different site), forcing the model to rely on structural and textural cues rather than absolute color values. This is critical given inherently ambiguous label boundaries (background/debris, stroma/smooth muscle, mucus overlap). All three orientation-safe augmentations (hflip, vflip, rotate90) are applied train-only to expand the effective sample size across 9 moderately imbalanced classes (ratio 1.63), covering the full 2D dihedral group and reducing overfitting risk on the smaller classes (7886, 8006 samples) without introducing orientation-dependent artifacts.

train_config.rationale: PathMNIST's 9-class histopathology task with 107k samples and mild 1.63x imbalance supports a compact 16-unit hidden layer and 128 batch size for stable, low-cost training. Standardize normalization and geometric augmentations (hflip/vflip/rotate90) reduce the need for heavy capacity. Class weighting is enabled to offset the mild imbalance. LR 1e-3 with weight decay 0.01 keeps optimization stable within the 8-epoch budget, avoiding overfitting on the small architecture.
